run.question:
Alertmanager alert KubePodNotReady (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-875zl since 2026-11-26T02:14:00Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert fires because the newly created pod of Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog cannot start: its container image reference quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1 does not exist in the registry ('failed to resolve reference ... not found'), so the container stays in ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff and the pod stays Pending and not-ready. The Deployment's container image was changed to that tag at 2026-11-26T02:13:41Z (managedFieldsSummary manager 'OpenAPI-Generator'), which created ReplicaSet product-catalog-7b499ffb4f and pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-875zl at that time. Observed facts: kube_pod_status_phase phase=Pending is 1 and kube_pod_status_ready condition=true is 0 for that pod from 02:14:00Z to 02:19:00Z; kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason shows ErrImagePull then ImagePullBackOff; kubelet emitted Warning Failed 'ErrImagePull' and 'ImagePullBackOff' events plus Normal BackOff (20 occurrences) up to 02:18:48Z. The rollout is a consequence of an invalid image reference in the Deployment, not a node, credential or feature-flag problem: busybox:latest was pulled successfully in the same pod at 02:13:42Z, the message says the reference was 'not found' rather than an authorization error, and every flag in otel-demo/flagd-config (including productCatalogFailure and productCatalogLockContention) has defaultVariant 'off'. Only the new pod is observed failing: the previous pod product-catalog-658dcdbc87-vnnxp stayed Ready=1, kube_deployment_status_replicas_available for product-catalog stayed 1 through 02:18:00Z, and the 50-minute product-catalog span aggregate returned only STATUS_CODE_UNSET with no ERROR status series, so no product-catalog request error impact was observed. A separate KubePodNotReady instance is also firing for itbench-observability/prometheus-kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus-0.

claims.text: Pod otel-demo/product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-875zl is Pending with Ready=False (reason ContainersNotReady, message 'containers with unready status: [product-catalog]'); its container 'product-catalog' is not ready with restartCount 0 and state.waiting.reason ImagePullBackOff and message 'Back-off pulling image "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1": ErrImagePull: rpc error: code = NotFound desc = failed to pull and unpack image ... failed to resolve reference ... not found'.

Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog has container 'product-catalog' image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1, observedGeneration 2, status replicas 2, readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1; its managedFieldsSummary shows manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' operation Update at 2026-11-26T02:13:41Z as the latest spec write, alongside helm Apply at 02:06:17Z.

Two ReplicaSets are owned by Deployment product-catalog: product-catalog-658dcdbc87 (created 02:06:18Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-product-catalog, 1 ready and available) and product-catalog-7b499ffb4f (created 02:13:41Z, image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1, replicas 1, ready and available null).

Events in otel-demo for this rollout and pod: Deployment product-catalog ScalingReplicaSet 'Scaled up replica set product-catalog-7b499ffb4f from 0 to 1' at 02:13:41Z; ReplicaSet product-catalog-7b499ffb4f SuccessfulCreate pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-875zl at 02:13:41Z; Pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-875zl Warning Failed 'Failed to pull image "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1": ... not found' (count 5, at 02:16:41Z), Warning Failed 'Error: ErrImagePull' (count 5, 02:16:41Z), Normal BackOff 'Back-off pulling image ...' (count 20, 02:18:48Z) and Warning Failed 'Error: ImagePullBackOff' (count 20, 02:18:48Z). No Warning event in otel-demo names another pod in this window.

kube_pod_status_phase for pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-875zl is phase=Pending value 1 (Running, Failed, Succeeded, Unknown all 0) at every sampled step from 2026-11-26T02:14:00Z to 02:19:00Z, and kube_pod_status_ready{condition="true"} for that pod is 0 at every sampled step from 02:14:00Z to 02:18:00Z.

kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason for container product-catalog in pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-875zl shows reason PodInitializing=1 at 02:14:00Z, reason ErrImagePull=1 at 02:15:00Z, and reason ImagePullBackOff=1 at 02:16:00Z, 02:17:00Z, 02:18:00Z and 02:19:00Z.

Alerting rule KubePodNotReady (group kubernetes-apps, severity warning, duration 300, keepFiringFor 0) has a firing instance for namespace otel-demo, pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-875zl with activeAt 2026-11-26T02:14:00Z; its annotation text says the pod 'has been in a non-ready state for longer than 15 minutes'.

The same KubePodNotReady rule also has a firing instance for pod prometheus-kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus-0 in namespace itbench-observability with activeAt 2026-11-26T02:03:30Z, a different pod and namespace from the alert under investigation.

Pod product-catalog-658dcdbc87-vnnxp (the running product-catalog instance) log streams: container wait-for-astronomy-db wrote 'astronomy-db (10.96.29.221:5432) open' at 2026-11-26T02:06:21Z; the product-catalog container produced 0 lines and neither container has a previous instance, so its own application output neither shows an error nor establishes health.

kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment="product-catalog"} stayed at 1 at every sampled step from 02:08:00Z to 02:18:00Z, and kube_pod_status_ready{condition="true"} was 1 for the older pod product-catalog-658dcdbc87-vnnxp at every step 02:08:00Z-02:18:00Z, so the product-catalog workload kept one ready replica while the new pod failed.

Aggregated over 01:29:10Z-02:19:10Z, traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name product-catalog returned a single series with status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET only; no ERROR-status product-catalog series appeared in that aggregate, so no product-catalog error-span impact is visible in this window (STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status and is not proof of success).

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config defines every flag with defaultVariant "off", including productCatalogFailure (defaultVariant off, with targeting that also resolves to off) and productCatalogLockContention (defaultVariant off), so no enabled feature-flag fault aimed at product-catalog is present in the configuration read.

Rejected: registry authentication or a missing image-pull secret caused the pull failure. The kubelet message reports the reference as 'not found' / 'failed to resolve reference', which is a NotFound lookup result, not an authorization error.

Rejected: node-level or general registry connectivity failure blocked image pulls. In the same pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-875zl on node kind-environment-worker, image busybox:latest was pulled successfully at 02:13:42Z ('Successfully pulled image "busybox:latest" in 472ms'), so only the specific reference quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1 failed.

The rollout was triggered by an external writer whose Kubernetes field-manager identity is 'OpenAPI-Generator', which last wrote the product-catalog Deployment spec at 02:13:41Z setting the container image to the nonexistent tag quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-amd64:1.0.0rc1; which tool or actor holds that identity, and whether the tag was ever intended to exist, is not determinable from the available sources.

Roll back Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog to the previously working image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-product-catalog (or use a tag that exists in the registry) so ReplicaSet product-catalog-7b499ffb4f and pod product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-875zl can start, then confirm pod readiness and that the Deployment reports no unavailableReplicas.

gaps: Who or what applied the image change at 2026-11-26T02:13:41Z is unknown: managedFieldsSummary records only the last write per manager (identity 'OpenAPI-Generator'), and the change_history integration is not available in this Run, so the acting user/service and the reason for the tag are unverified.

The alert text ('non-ready for longer than 15 minutes') does not match the observable timeline: the rule's own duration is 300s, the pod was created at 02:13:41Z, and KubePodNotReady activeAt is recorded as 02:14:00Z, earlier than either threshold; the reason for the recorded activeAt is unexplained.
Whether this image tag exists anywhere, or was mistyped versus removed, cannot be verified: the only registry evidence is the kubelet's NotFound message.
The product-catalog container of the failing pod never started, so it produced no logs; no application-level evidence from that container exists.
Service otel-demo/product-catalog and its endpoints were not inspected, so whether the not-ready pod was excluded from or included in routing was not checked.

Trace coverage is incomplete: traces_search for product-catalog over 01:44-02:19Z returned RESULT_TOO_LARGE and was not read back, and traces_search_by_tags with error=true over that window returned status no_data (0 traces matched), so per-span status and latency for product-catalog were only examined through aggregated span metrics, and the tag search matched nothing rather than proving no errors.
next_steps: Confirm which actor (CI/CD, benchmark harness or operator) owns the field-manager identity 'OpenAPI-Generator' and revert the product-catalog image to a tag that resolves in the registry.

Watch kube_pod_status_ready and kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason for product-catalog-7b499ffb4f-875zl after the image is corrected, and confirm ReplicaSet product-catalog-658dcdbc87 is scaled down only after the new pod is Ready.
Align the KubePodNotReady alert annotation ('15 minutes') with the rule's 300s duration to avoid misleading alert text.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

notes: This tool has no time range: it shows Prometheus's state at the moment of the query, which can be after the authorized window; it cannot show the state when the incident happened.

rules.name: KubePodNotReady
rules.query: sum by (namespace, pod, job, cluster) (max by (namespace, pod, job, cluster) (kube_pod_status_phase{job="kube-state-metrics",namespace=~".*",phase=~"Pending|Unknown"} or (kube_pod_status_phase{job="kube-state-metrics",namespace=~".*",phase="Running"} == 1 and on (namespace, pod, cluster) kube_pod_status_ready{condition="true",job="kube-state-metrics",namespace=~".*"} == 0)) * on (namespace, pod, cluster) group_left () topk by (namespace, pod, cluster) (1, max by (namespace, pod, owner_kind, cluster) (kube_pod_owner{owner_kind!="Job"}))) > 0 unless on (namespace, pod, cluster) kube_pod_status_reason{job="kube-state-metrics",namespace=~".*",reason="SchedulingGated"} == 1

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
